Formal is exhaustive but struggles with large designs and long sequences; simulation scales but is never complete.
what is the cone of influence of a check: The cone of influence of a property is the set of signals and state elements that can affect it, found by tracing backwards from the signals in the property through the logic to the inputs. Formal tools only analyse this cone and ignore everything else, which reduces the state space. Keeping properties local and cutting irrelevant logic keeps the cone small and the proof tractable.
given verilog code describe the hardware: Map each construct to hardware: continuous assigns and always @(*) blocks become combinational logic (operators become adders, comparators and gates; if and case become multiplexers or priority logic); always @(posedge clk) blocks become flip-flops with the logic feeding their D inputs; signals not assigned in every branch of combinational logic become latches; for loops unroll into repeated logic. Draw the resulting registers and logic between them.
explain the regions of operation of a cm: Plot Vout against Vin. Region A (Vin < Vtn): NMOS off, PMOS linear, Vout = VDD. Region B: NMOS saturated, PMOS linear, output starts to fall. Region C (around the switching threshold VM): both saturated, very high gain, steep drop. Region D: NMOS linear, PMOS saturated. Region E (Vin > VDD - |Vtp|): PMOS off, NMOS linear, Vout = 0. VM is set by the PMOS-to-NMOS strength ratio; the slope of -1 points define VIL and VIH and the noise margins.
implement a ring oscillator how do you s: Connect an odd number of inverters in a loop: no stable state exists, so it oscillates with period T = 2 N td, where N is the number of stages and td the delay per inverter. To slow it down, add more stages (keeping the count odd), add load capacitance or use current-starved inverters (limit each stage's current with extra transistors controlled by a bias voltage, which makes it a VCO), or divide the output frequency with a counter.
c1 10 pf and c2 1 pf are in series with: Assuming both capacitors start uncharged, in series they get the same charge, so the voltages split in inverse proportion to capacitance: V across C2 = 5 V x C1 / (C1 + C2) = 5 x 10 / 11 = about 4.55 V, and about 0.45 V across C1. The smaller capacitor takes most of the voltage. If they were pre-charged, charge conservation on the node between them would decide the answer instead.
given 11 minterms derive the logic funct: Write the function as a sum of the given minterms, then simplify. With 11 of 16 minterms for 4 variables, it is often easier to simplify the complement: group the 5 missing minterms (the maxterms) in a K-map to get F as a product of sums, or group the 1s with the largest possible blocks of 8, 4 and 2, using wrap-around adjacency. Check the result against a few minterms.
compare fir and iir filters: An FIR (finite impulse response) filter uses only current and past inputs: y[n] = sum of b_k x[n-k]. It is always stable, can have exactly linear phase, and is easy to pipeline, but needs many taps for sharp responses. An IIR (infinite impulse response) filter also feeds back past outputs, so it reaches a sharp response with far fewer coefficients and less hardware, but it can be unstable, has non-linear phase, and is sensitive to coefficient quantisation and overflow.
draw the logic for y abc a bc: y = abc + a'bc' = b (ac + a'c') = b AND (a XNOR c). Draw an XNOR gate on a and c, then an AND gate with b. With basic gates: two AND3 gates (a, b, c) and (a', b, c') with inverters on a and c, feeding an OR2.
how do a sampling scope and a real time: A real-time scope digitises the signal continuously at a sample rate several times its bandwidth, so it captures single-shot events. A sampling (equivalent-time) scope takes one sample per trigger at a slightly shifted delay each time and rebuilds a repetitive waveform, reaching very high bandwidths (tens of GHz) with slow ADCs, but it only works for repetitive signals such as eye diagrams.
how do you debug failing serial and para: Start by deciding whether the problem is in shift or capture. Run a chain integrity (flush) test first: if it fails in serial simulation, check scan connectivity, clocks and reset during shift, lockup latches and test-mode setup. Parallel simulation forces the chain values directly, so a pattern that passes in parallel but fails in serial points to shift problems; failures in both point to capture problems: timing (need SDF annotation), uninitialised X sources, clocking, constraints mismatch with ATPG, or bus contention. Compare the failing flop and cycle with the ATPG expected values.
how do you verify the bit error rate ber: Transmit a known PRBS pattern (PRBS7, PRBS31) through the link, and use a checker on the receive side that locks to the sequence and counts bit errors over a large number of bits. BER = errors / bits. To claim 1e-12 with 95% confidence and zero errors you need about 3e12 bits. Sweep jitter, attenuation and loss (stressed eye), and use the eye diagram, bathtub curves and on-die eye monitors to estimate margin; in simulation, check with statistical channel analysis.
in mbist what are the pros and cons of s: A shared comparator is placed in the MBIST controller and compares data from several memories in turn: less area and fewer wires, but memories are tested sequentially (longer test time) and the routing of read data back to the controller can be long. Local comparators sit next to each memory: they allow parallel testing and faster diagnosis, at a higher area cost. The choice trades area against test time and power.
what atpg drc violations do you know: Typical scan DRC violations: clocks not controllable from top-level pins during test, asynchronous set or reset not controllable, uncontrolled latches or transparent latches in the scan path, combinational feedback loops, tri-state bus contention, flops not on a scan chain, X sources reaching scan flops (uninitialised memories or black boxes), clock-domain issues between chains, and shift-path problems. They are fixed with test points, test-mode muxes and constraints.
what are static class members: A static class member (a static property or method) belongs to the class rather than to each object: there is a single copy shared by all instances. A static property can count objects created or hold a shared configuration; static methods can only access static members and can be called with class_name::method() without creating an object. The UVM singleton patterns use this.
what is ir drop: IR drop is the voltage lost along the power and ground network because of its resistance (V = I R), so cells see less than the nominal supply. Static IR drop uses average currents; dynamic IR drop uses simultaneous switching current peaks. Lower supply slows cells and can cause timing failures or functional errors. Fix it with a denser or wider power grid, more vias and pins, decap cells, and spreading high-activity logic.
what is a pll: A phase-locked loop generates a stable, high-frequency clock locked to a reference. A phase-frequency detector compares the reference with the divided output, a charge pump and loop filter turn the error into a control voltage, and a voltage-controlled oscillator produces the output; a divider by N in the feedback makes fout = N x fref. PLLs are used for clock multiplication, de-skewing, frequency synthesis and clock recovery.
what is a pull up resistor used for: A pull-up resistor ties a line weakly to VDD so it has a defined high level when nothing drives it, for example a floating input, a button, or an open-drain or open-collector bus such as I2C, where devices only pull low. Its value trades rise time (smaller is faster) against current and power when the line is pulled low.
what is gate level simulation used for: Gate-level simulation runs the synthesized or post-layout netlist, often with SDF timing back-annotated. It catches synthesis-simulation mismatches, X-propagation and reset problems that RTL hides, scan and DFT behaviour, timing issues on paths that STA was told to ignore (false or multicycle paths, asynchronous logic), and power-up sequences, and it gives switching activity for power analysis.
what is the difference between continuou: Continuous assignments (assign y = a & b;) drive a net all the time: whenever a right-hand side changes, the net updates; they model combinational logic and wires. Procedural assignments happen inside always or initial blocks when that code executes, and assign to variables (reg or logic), which keep their value until assigned again. Procedural assignments can be blocking (=) or non-blocking (<=) and can model both combinational and sequential logic.
given a block diagram of a protocol bloc: Write a class (or a module with tasks) that converts transactions to pin activity and back. Define a transaction class with the fields from the protocol; give the transactor a virtual interface to the block's signals; implement a drive task that waits for the bus to be ready, drives the fields with the right timing (valid, ready, data phases), and waits for completion, and a monitor task that samples the pins and builds transactions. Use a clocking block for clean sampling and a mailbox to exchange transactions with the testbench.
how does systemverilog differ from veril: SystemVerilog extends Verilog for both design and verification. For design: logic, enum, struct, typedef, packages, interfaces, always_ff, always_comb and always_latch, and unique and priority case. For verification: classes and OOP, constrained random generation, functional coverage (covergroups), assertions (SVA), dynamic and associative arrays and queues, mailboxes and semaphores, fork-join variants, and clocking blocks. It is the base of UVM.
explain the operating regions of a mosfe: Cut-off (VGS < Vt): no channel, the transistor is off. Linear or triode (VGS > Vt and VDS < VGS - Vt): it acts like a voltage-controlled resistor. Saturation (VDS > VGS - Vt): the current depends mainly on VGS, so it acts as a current source. Digital circuits use the transistor as a switch, moving between cut-off and linear. Analog circuits bias it in saturation, where it gives gain (amplifiers, current mirrors, differential pairs).
for a diode circuit with vd 0 7 v and rc: Without the figure, the common case is a diode clipper or peak detector. For a series diode with R and C forming a peak detector: when Vi exceeds Vr + 0.7 V the diode conducts and Vr follows Vi - 0.7 V; when Vi falls, the diode turns off and the capacitor holds Vr, decaying with time constant RC = 1 us. For a shunt clipper, Vr follows Vi until it reaches 0.7 V (plus any reference) and then stays clamped. Sketch the transfer curve with the 0.7 V breakpoints.
with a sine wave on an inverter s input: As the sine rises from 0: near 0 V the NMOS is off and the PMOS is in its linear region (output high). As Vin passes Vtn the NMOS turns on in saturation while the PMOS is still linear. Around the switching threshold both are saturated. Then the NMOS moves into linear and the PMOS into saturation, and above VDD - |Vtp| the PMOS turns off with the NMOS linear (output low). On the falling half the sequence reverses.
what is instruction pipelining: Instruction pipelining divides instruction execution into stages (fetch, decode, execute, memory access, write-back) with registers between them, so while one instruction executes, the next is being decoded and the one after is being fetched. Throughput approaches one instruction per cycle and the clock can be faster, although each instruction's latency stays the same; hazards need forwarding, stalls and branch prediction.
c1 holds 1 c of charge at 1 v c2 is an u: Charge is conserved: the 1 C shares between two 1 F capacitors, so each ends at 0.5 V. The initial energy is 0.5 x 1 x 1^2 = 0.5 J; the final energy is 2 x 0.5 x 1 x 0.5^2 = 0.25 J. So 0.25 J, half of the initial energy, is dissipated in R, whatever the value of R (R only changes how fast it happens).
draw a circuit that generates the repeat: Both sequences repeat every 3 steps, and the second is the bitwise complement of the first. Use a mod-3 counter (2 flops counting 0, 1, 2) and decode it: count 0 gives 11, 1 gives 01, 2 gives 10. Then the outputs are y1 = (count != 1), y0 = (count != 2), and the second sequence is ~y1, ~y0. You can also build it directly as a 2-flop state machine whose state is the output pattern.
explain false paths and half cycle paths: A false path is a timing path that can never be exercised functionally (for example between asynchronous clock domains with synchronisers, or test-only logic), so STA is told to ignore it with set_false_path. A half-cycle path launches on one edge of the clock and captures on the opposite edge (for example a negative-edge flop feeding a positive-edge flop), so it only has half a period for setup, but more room for hold.
find the steady state output across a pa: If the parallel RC is driven directly by an ideal voltage source, the voltage across it is just Vi = Vp cos(t/RC). The likely intent is a source resistor R in series with the parallel RC: with omega = 1/RC the capacitor's impedance is -jR, the parallel combination is R/(1 + j), and the divider gives H = 1/(2 + j), so the output is Vp/sqrt(5) cos(t/RC - 26.6 degrees), about 0.45 Vp.
implement a state machine for sequence d: Draw the state diagram: one state per prefix of the pattern matched so far. On each input, go to the state for the longest suffix that is still a prefix (that handles overlaps). Choose Mealy (output on the transition, one state fewer, output in the same cycle) or Moore (output in a state, one cycle later, glitch-free). Code it with a state register in always_ff and next-state and output logic in always_comb with a default branch, then test with a stream containing overlapping matches.
what are big endian and little endian: They are the byte order of multi-byte words in memory. Big-endian stores the most significant byte at the lowest address (network order); little-endian stores the least significant byte first (x86, and most Arm systems). For 0x12345678 at address 0, big-endian memory holds 12 34 56 78 and little-endian holds 78 56 34 12. It matters when data crosses buses, files or networks.
what are parasitics what is em ir and wh: Parasitics are the unwanted resistance, capacitance and inductance of wires and devices, extracted from the layout (SPEF) and added to timing and power analysis. EM (electromigration) is the gradual movement of metal atoms caused by high current density, which creates voids (opens) or hillocks (shorts) over time. IR drop is the voltage loss on the power grid due to its resistance. EM causes long-term wear-out failures; IR drop slows or breaks circuits; both are signed off with current-density and voltage-drop limits.
what are the inputs to a timing engine: The gate-level netlist, the timing libraries (Liberty .lib files) for the cells at each corner, the constraints (SDC: clocks, input and output delays, exceptions), the parasitics (SPEF or SDF from extraction, or wire-load models before layout), and settings for operating conditions, derates or OCV and AOCV/POCV tables. For multi-mode multi-corner analysis, a set of each per scenario.
what are timing arcs: A timing arc is a delay path inside a cell or a net from one pin to another, described in the Liberty library. Combinational arcs go from an input to an output (positive unate, negative unate or non-unate). Sequential arcs go from the clock pin to the output (clock-to-Q), and timing-check arcs describe setup, hold, recovery and removal between data and clock. Net arcs connect a driver to its loads. STA traces paths by chaining arcs.
what is the difference between a task an: A function executes in zero simulation time, cannot contain delays or event controls, must return a value (or be void in SystemVerilog) and can only call other functions; it is used for combinational calculations. A task can consume time (#delay, @(posedge clk), wait), has no return value but can have output arguments, and can call functions and other tasks; it is used for stimulus sequences and bus protocols.
describe the hierarchy of a systemverilo: Top module (DUT, interface, clock and reset, run_test), then the test (configures and starts sequences), the environment (agents, scoreboard, coverage), the agents (sequencer, driver, monitor per interface), and the transactions (sequence items) and sequences. Without UVM: a top module, interface, program or testbench module, with a generator, driver, monitor, scoreboard and checker classes connected by mailboxes.
explain inheritance polymorphism and abs: Inheritance: a class extends a base class and reuses its properties and methods (class burst_txn extends txn). Polymorphism: a base-class handle can point to a derived object, and virtual methods run the derived version at run time, so generic code works with any derived type. Abstraction: virtual classes and pure virtual methods define an interface that derived classes must implement, hiding implementation details. These are the basis of reusable testbenches and UVM.
explain the systemverilog event schedule: Each time step is divided into regions. Preponed: values are sampled for assertions. Active: blocking assignments, continuous assignments and $display run. Inactive: #0 events. NBA: non-blocking assignments update. Observed: assertions are evaluated. Reactive: program blocks and assertion action blocks run. Postponed: $strobe and $monitor print final values. This ordering, with sampling before changes, is what lets clocking blocks and assertions avoid races with the design.
explain the uvm phases and why each matt: Build phases run first: build_phase (top-down: create components and get config), connect_phase (bottom-up: connect TLM ports), end_of_elaboration_phase (check topology), start_of_simulation_phase. Then run_phase, which is a task and consumes time (in parallel with the run-time sub-phases reset, configure, main and shutdown). Cleanup phases follow: extract_phase, check_phase, report_phase, final_phase. Phasing makes every component build, connect, run and report in a consistent order; objections control when run_phase ends.
what are the uvm phases and their proper: Function phases take no simulation time: build (top-down), connect, end_of_elaboration, start_of_simulation, extract, check, report and final (bottom-up). Task phases consume time: run_phase, and the run-time sub-phases pre_reset, reset, configure, main and shutdown with pre and post variants, which run in parallel with run_phase. A phase ends when all raised objections are dropped. Build is top-down so parents create children; the others are bottom-up.
what are the factory override methods in: Type overrides replace every instance of a type: set_type_override_by_type(orig::get_type(), new::get_type()) or set_type_override_by_name(). Instance overrides replace only the objects created at a given hierarchy path: set_inst_override_by_type(path, orig::get_type(), new::get_type()) or by name. They only take effect for objects created with type_id::create() and must be set before the build_phase creates them. Instance overrides take priority over type overrides.
design an sram cell and explain how it w: The standard 6T SRAM cell is two cross-coupled inverters that hold a bit and its complement, plus two NMOS access transistors connecting the storage nodes to the bit lines BL and BLB, controlled by the word line. To read, precharge both bit lines high and raise the word line; the side storing 0 slowly discharges its bit line and a sense amplifier detects the small difference. To write, drive BL and BLB to opposite values and raise the word line; the strong drivers overpower the cell. Sizing matters: the pull-down must be stronger than the access transistor for read stability, and the access transistor stronger than the pull-up for writability.
what is the difference between sram and: SRAM stores each bit in a 6-transistor latch: fast, no refresh, compatible with the logic process, but large (low density) and costly; it is used for caches and register files. DRAM stores each bit as charge on a capacitor with one access transistor (1T1C): very dense and cheap per bit, but slower, reads are destructive, and the charge leaks so it must be refreshed every few tens of milliseconds; it is used for main memory and needs a special process.
what is the difference between a microco: A microprocessor is a CPU on a chip that needs external memory and peripherals; a microcontroller integrates the CPU with program memory (ROM or flash), RAM, timers, serial ports and GPIO on one chip for embedded control. The 8051 is an 8-bit microcontroller with an 8-bit ALU and accumulator, 4 KB of on-chip ROM, 128 bytes of RAM including four register banks, 4 parallel I/O ports (P0 to P3), two 16-bit timers or counters, a full-duplex UART, 5 interrupt sources, a 16-bit program counter and data pointer, and a Harvard memory organisation.
explain rc and rl filters: An RC low-pass filter has R in series and C to ground: the capacitor shorts high frequencies, so the cut-off is fc = 1/(2 pi R C) with -20 dB/decade roll-off. Swapping them (C in series, R to ground) makes a high-pass filter. An RL filter does the same with an inductor, whose impedance rises with frequency: R in series with L to ground is a high-pass, L in series with R to ground is a low-pass, with fc = R/(2 pi L). Both are first-order filters with a 45 degree phase shift at fc.
how do you multiply binary numbers: Like long multiplication in decimal, but each partial product is either 0 or the multiplicand shifted: for each 1 bit of the multiplier, add the multiplicand shifted left by that bit's position. For example 101 x 11 = 101 + 1010 = 1111 (5 x 3 = 15). In hardware this is an array multiplier (AND gates for partial products plus adders), a sequential shift-and-add multiplier, or a fast Wallace or Dadda tree with Booth encoding to reduce the number of partial products. For signed numbers use Booth or sign extension.
walk through the complete asic flow: Specification and architecture, micro-architecture, RTL coding, functional verification (simulation, formal, emulation), lint, CDC and RDC checks, then synthesis with constraints into a netlist, DFT insertion (scan, MBIST), and logical equivalence checking. Physical design: floorplan and power grid, placement, clock tree synthesis, routing, with timing optimisation at each step. Sign-off: STA across corners and modes, IR drop and EM, signal integrity, physical verification (DRC, LVS, antenna, density), and final equivalence. Then tape-out of GDSII, fabrication, packaging, post-silicon validation and production test.
what is an rlc network explain its compo: An RLC network combines a resistor (dissipates energy, V = IR), an inductor (stores energy in a magnetic field, V = L di/dt, impedance j omega L) and a capacitor (stores energy in an electric field, I = C dV/dt, impedance 1/(j omega C)). Together they form a second-order system with a resonant frequency f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(LC)) where the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, and a damping set by R and the quality factor Q. They are used in filters, tuned circuits and oscillators, and model power delivery networks and transmission lines.
what is skin effect and how does it affe: At high frequencies, alternating current crowds toward the surface of a conductor, flowing in a layer whose depth decreases with the square root of frequency (about 2 um in copper at 1 GHz). The effective cross-section shrinks, so the resistance and loss of PCB traces rise with frequency, attenuating fast signals and degrading the eye. Designers use wider traces, smoother copper, low-loss dielectrics, shorter routes and equalisation in the SerDes to compensate.
what is the difference between drc and l: DRC (design rule check) verifies that the layout geometry obeys the foundry's manufacturing rules: minimum width, spacing, enclosure, density and antenna rules. LVS (layout versus schematic) extracts the circuit from the layout and checks that it matches the netlist: same devices, connections and sizes, with no shorts or opens. DRC makes the chip manufacturable; LVS makes sure what is manufactured is the intended circuit.
what power reduction techniques do you k: Clock gating, multi-Vt cell assignment, power gating with isolation and retention cells, multiple voltage domains, dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, operand isolation, low-power memory modes and memory banking, reducing switching activity through encoding and glitch reduction, and architectural choices such as parallelism at lower voltage. Implementation is driven by UPF power intent and verified with power-aware simulation.
how do you protect a circuit against vol: Use clamping and filtering: TVS diodes or Zener clamps at the inputs, series resistors or ferrite beads to limit current, RC snubbers across switching elements, flyback diodes across inductive loads, decoupling and bulk capacitors on supplies, MOVs or gas discharge tubes for high-energy surges, and good layout (short return paths, ground planes). On chip, ESD structures with diodes to the supply rails protect the IO pins.
design a two stage pipelined alu that ex: Stage 1 fetches the next instruction word from the list and decodes it: the opcode selects the operation and the fields select source registers or immediates, which are read from the register file into a pipeline register. Stage 2 executes the ALU operation and writes the result back to the register file. Because an instruction may use the result of the one just before, add forwarding from the stage-2 result to the stage-1 operand outputs (or stall one cycle). Verify with a reference model that runs the same hex program.
how do you check whether a system is lit: Store a known multi-byte value and look at the byte at its lowest address. In C: uint32_t x = 1; if (*(uint8_t *)&x == 1) it is little-endian, else big-endian. A union of a uint32_t and a uint8_t[4] works too. In hardware, write a 32-bit word over the bus and read it back byte by byte to see which byte lane holds the least significant byte.
what happens during synthesis of an fpga: Synthesis turns the HDL into a netlist of FPGA primitives: it infers logic, optimises it, and maps it to LUTs, flip-flops, carry chains, block RAMs and DSP slices. Implementation then places those primitives onto specific sites in the device, routes the connections through the programmable interconnect, runs timing analysis against the constraints, and finally generates the bitstream that configures the FPGA.
which physical cmos parameters affect pr: Supply voltage (higher VDD is faster), threshold voltage (lower Vt is faster but leaks more), transistor width and length (wider and shorter is faster), gate oxide thickness and carrier mobility, load capacitance (fan-out, wire and diffusion capacitance), input slew, temperature, and process variation. Delay is roughly C VDD / I_on, so anything that increases drive current or reduces capacitance speeds the gate up.
explain the function of a muxed scan fli: A muxed scan flip-flop is a normal D flip-flop with a 2:1 multiplexer on its D input. When scan enable (SE) is 0, the mux passes the functional data D, so the flop works normally and captures the circuit's response. When SE is 1, it passes the scan input SI from the previous flop's output, so all scan flops form a shift register (a scan chain) to load test patterns and unload results. It costs a mux delay on the data path.
in equivalence checking how do you handl: Constrain it. When comparing RTL (without scan) against a scan-inserted netlist, set scan enable to its functional value (0) with a constant constraint, so the scan muxes always select functional data and the extra scan path does not appear as a difference. Similarly tie test-mode signals to functional values, and give the tool any scan-chain reordering information so register mapping works.
how does pvt affect delay: Process: fast corners (FF) have stronger transistors and shorter delay, slow corners (SS) longer delay. Voltage: a higher supply increases drive current and reduces delay. Temperature: in older nodes delay increases with temperature (lower mobility); in advanced nodes at low voltage, temperature inversion can make cold the slower corner because Vt rises. STA therefore checks setup at the slow corner and hold at the fast corner, plus on-chip variation derates.
what are the components of power dissipa: Dynamic switching power alpha C V^2 f, from charging and discharging capacitances: reduce it with clock gating, lower voltage and frequency, less switching activity and smaller capacitance. Short-circuit power during transitions when both networks conduct: keep input slews sharp. Static leakage power (subthreshold, gate and junction leakage): reduce it with high-Vt cells, power gating, body biasing and lower supply. Voltage is the strongest lever because of the V^2 term.
draw how an fpga tool turns a block of c: Draw it in stages. The HDL code is elaborated into generic logic (operators, muxes, registers); synthesis optimises it and maps it to FPGA primitives such as LUTs (each holding a small truth table), flip-flops, carry chains, block RAM and DSP blocks; placement assigns those to physical sites; routing connects them through programmable switch boxes; timing analysis checks the paths; and the bitstream writes the LUT contents and routing configuration into the device.
how would your design change for a diffe: Explain the trade-off. A faster specification usually means pipelining (more registers, more latency, more area) or parallel hardware; a lower-cost one means resource sharing or a serial implementation (fewer LUTs or gates but more cycles and a longer critical path through shared multiplexers). Wider data increases area and carry-chain delay. Quantify with the critical path (logic levels and propagation delay) and resource counts (LUTs, flops, DSPs) for each option.
write a simple register in systemverilog: module reg8 (input logic clk, rst_n, en, input logic [7:0] d, output logic [7:0] q); always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) if (!rst_n) q <= '0; else if (en) q <= d; endmodule. It has an asynchronous active-low reset and a load enable; always_ff tells tools this must be a flip-flop.
explain the basic architecture of a micr: A microcontroller combines a CPU core with on-chip program memory (flash or ROM), data RAM, timers, ADCs, serial interfaces (UART, SPI, I2C), GPIO, an interrupt controller and a clock system on one chip, designed for embedded control at low cost and power. A microprocessor contains mainly the CPU (and caches) and relies on external memory and peripheral chips, optimised for high performance general computing.
why build a 16 bit microcontroller inste: A native 16-bit core processes 16-bit data in one instruction instead of several (cascading 8-bit operations needs carries between them and more instructions), addresses more memory directly, and gives better code density and performance per clock. Cascading two 8-bit parts adds glue logic, synchronisation and software complexity, and costs more board area and power than one integrated 16-bit device.
explain the keywords volatile const and: volatile tells the compiler a variable can change outside the program's control (hardware registers, ISR-shared variables), so it must reread it on every access and not optimise reads or writes away. const makes a variable read-only, so the compiler can place it in flash and catch accidental writes. static inside a function keeps the variable's value between calls; at file scope it limits visibility to that file (internal linkage).
what is the difference between von neuma: Von Neumann uses one memory and one bus for both instructions and data: simpler and flexible (programs can be loaded as data), but instruction and data accesses compete for the bus (the Von Neumann bottleneck); typical of general-purpose computers. Harvard uses separate memories and buses, so an instruction fetch and a data access happen at the same time: faster and common in DSPs and microcontrollers such as the 8051 and AVR. Modern CPUs are modified Harvard: split L1 caches over a unified memory.
how do you handle timing paths that cros: Mark them as asynchronous in STA (set_clock_groups -asynchronous or set_false_path) so the tool does not try to time them, and make them safe in the design instead: two-flop synchronisers for single bits, handshakes or asynchronous FIFOs with Gray-coded pointers for buses, and pulse synchronisers for pulses. Then constrain the remaining requirements, such as a max delay or skew between bits of a Gray bus (set_max_delay -datapath_only), and run CDC verification to prove every crossing is synchronised.
draw a nand gate in cmos: Draw two PMOS transistors in parallel from VDD to the output, gates on A and B, and two NMOS transistors in series from the output to ground, gates on A and B. The output is pulled low only when both A and B are 1 (both NMOS on, both PMOS off); otherwise at least one PMOS pulls it high. Size the series NMOS about twice as wide to balance the pull-down with the pull-up.
explain the 5 stage pipeline the types o: The five stages are fetch, decode, execute, memory and write-back. Hazards: structural (shared resources), data (RAW, plus WAR and WAW in out-of-order designs) and control (branches). RAW data hazards are fixed by forwarding from the EX/MEM and MEM/WB registers, with a one-cycle stall for a load followed by a use. To go beyond five stages, split the slow stages (cache access, decode, multiply) into more stages for a higher clock (superpipelining), and add better branch prediction because the mispredict penalty grows, or go superscalar and out of order.
how would you verify a multi level cache: Build a reference memory model and a coherence-aware scoreboard that knows the ordering rules, with agents on every master port and on the memory side. Drive random traffic from all masters concurrently, aimed at a small set of addresses to force sharing, evictions and conflicts, plus directed tests for fills, write-backs, coherence transitions, snoops and races. Add assertions on protocol and invariants (for example a single writable copy), check data on every read against the model, and close coverage on cache states, transitions crossed with masters, and hit or miss at each level.
what are a cache and a tlb: A cache is a small, fast memory that keeps copies of recently used data and instructions close to the processor, so most accesses avoid slow main memory. A TLB (translation lookaside buffer) is a small cache of virtual-to-physical address translations from the page tables, so most memory accesses do not need a page table walk. Both rely on locality; a TLB miss costs a page walk, a cache miss costs a trip to the next memory level.
what is virtual memory: Virtual memory is an abstraction in which each program sees its own large, private address space. The hardware MMU translates virtual addresses to physical memory in pages using page tables set up by the operating system; pages not in memory can live on disk and are loaded on a page fault. It gives isolation, protection, flexible allocation and the ability to run programs larger than physical memory.
how is a flip flop replaced with a scan: The DFT tool replaces each ordinary flip-flop with a scan flip-flop from the library, which adds a multiplexer in front of D with a scan enable (SE) and a scan input (SI); some libraries use clocked-scan or LSSD styles instead. The tool then stitches the flops into chains by connecting each Q (or a dedicated SO) to the next flop's SI, connects SE and the scan ports to top-level pins, inserts lockup latches between clock domains, and verifies the chains with DRC.
add two numbers without using the or ope: Use bitwise logic as a hardware adder does: XOR gives the sum without carries and AND shifted left gives the carries. Repeat until there are no carries: while (b != 0) { carry = (a & b) << 1; a = a ^ b; b = carry; } return a;. This loop takes at most as many iterations as there are bits.
build circuits using decoders and multip: A decoder with n inputs produces all 2^n minterms, so any function of those inputs is an OR of the selected decoder outputs (for example a full adder from a 3-to-8 decoder and two OR gates). A 2^n:1 multiplexer can implement any n-variable function by tying its data inputs to the truth table values, or any (n+1)-variable function by using the last variable, its complement or constants as data inputs. Larger muxes and decoders are built by cascading smaller ones.
compare risc and cisc instruction sets w: RISC (Arm, RISC-V, MIPS) uses a small set of simple, fixed-length instructions, load-store memory access and many registers: easy to decode and pipeline, low power, but more instructions per program. CISC (x86) has many complex, variable-length instructions with memory operands: compact code and fewer instructions, but complex decode; modern x86 cores translate them into RISC-like micro-ops internally. Today the difference is mostly in decode and ecosystem rather than performance.
explain how adcs and dacs work: A DAC turns a digital code into a voltage or current, using weighted resistors or currents, an R-2R ladder, a string of resistors, or delta-sigma modulation followed by filtering. An ADC samples the analog input with a sample-and-hold and quantises it into a code: a flash ADC compares against all levels at once, a SAR ADC performs a binary search using an internal DAC, a pipelined ADC resolves a few bits per stage, and a sigma-delta ADC oversamples and filters. Key specs are resolution, sample rate, SNR and linearity.
given two strings of 4 ascii characters: Compare the strings like 32-bit numbers: concatenate the four bytes with the first character as the most significant byte and use one 32-bit unsigned comparator, because lexicographic order on ASCII equals numeric order on the packed word. Or compare byte by byte from the first character: the first unequal byte decides, using four 8-bit comparators and priority logic. Output greater, equal and less.
how are delays characterized using a wir: Before layout there are no real wires, so a wire load model estimates a net's capacitance and resistance from its fan-out (and the block area), using lookup tables in the library: capacitance and resistance per unit length times an estimated length per fan-out. The synthesis tool adds the estimated wire capacitance to the pin loads and computes cell delay from the library tables with that load. WLMs are inaccurate in deep submicron designs, so physical synthesis or topographical mode is used instead.
how do you compute net interconnect dela: Extract the routed wire's geometry and use the technology file's per-unit-length resistance (from sheet resistance, width and layer) and capacitance (area, fringe and coupling, per layer and spacing) to build an RC network, written to SPEF. The delay is then computed with models such as the Elmore delay (the sum of each resistance times the downstream capacitance) or more accurate methods (AWE, Arnoldi), together with the driver's output model. Via resistances are added for layer changes.
how do you stop the tool from using cert: Mark them dont_use in the synthesis and place-and-route tools (set_dont_use [get_lib_cells lib/CELL*]), or remove them from the target library list. To keep particular instances from being changed, use set_dont_touch. Common examples are very weak or strong drive cells, cells with poor reliability, and scan or special cells that should not be used in functional logic.
how would you go about testing a chip wh: Start with the basics: power up with current limits and check supply currents, clocks and reset, and run a scan chain integrity test to confirm the test access works. Then structural tests (scan ATPG, at-speed transition tests, MBIST, IO and analog block tests), then functional and system tests with the real software, followed by characterisation across voltage, temperature and frequency (shmoo plots). Write a test plan from the spec first, and debug failures with diagnosis tools.
how would you insert voltage islands for: Group the macros by voltage domain and place them close to their power domain to keep crossings few and short. Every signal crossing between voltage islands needs a level shifter (and an isolation cell if the source can be switched off), placed at the domain boundary or near the receiver. To save resources, keep crossings to a small set of buses, share always-on routing, use combined level-shifter-isolation cells, and route the island's supply rings and switches only where needed. Capture it all in UPF.
what factors improve the propagation del: Higher drive strength (wider transistors), lower threshold voltage cells, higher supply voltage, lower load capacitance (fewer fan-outs, shorter wires), sharper input slew, fewer series transistors (prefer NAND to NOR, avoid tall stacks), a smaller internal parasitic capacitance through good layout, and logic restructuring to reduce logic depth. Each comes with area, power or leakage costs.
what is ram and what types of ram are th: RAM (random access memory) can be read and written at any address in roughly the same time and is usually volatile. The main types are SRAM (static, 6T latches, fast, used for caches and registers) and DRAM (dynamic, capacitor cells needing refresh, dense, used for main memory, in variants such as DDR, LPDDR, GDDR and HBM). Non-volatile random-access variants include MRAM, FRAM and ReRAM. On chip there are single-port, dual-port and register-file memories.
what is a pull up what is high impedance: A pull-up is a resistor (or weak transistor) to VDD that gives a line a default high level when no device drives it, used on open-drain buses and floating inputs. High impedance (Z) is the state of an output that is not driving at all, with both transistors off, so it neither sources nor sinks current and another device can drive the line; it is the third state of a tri-state buffer.
what is the difference between a mosfet: A MOSFET is voltage-controlled: the gate voltage sets the channel conductance, with almost no DC gate current, so it has very high input impedance, low static power and dense integration, which is why it dominates digital logic. A BJT is current-controlled: a small base current controls a larger collector current; it has higher transconductance, better matching and higher gain per current, and is used in analog, RF and high-current applications, but it draws base current and is less dense.
why are power stripes routed in the top: The top metal layers are the thickest and widest, so they have the lowest resistance, which minimises IR drop and electromigration for high power currents. Putting the global power grid there also leaves the lower, finer layers free for dense signal routing, and the top layers connect directly to the bumps or pads. Power then reaches cells through via stacks down to the standard cell rails.
write assembly that leaves r3 r1 r2 usin: Use shift-and-add (generic RISC syntax): r3 = 0; loop: if the low bit of r2 is 1, add r1 to r3; shift r1 left by one; shift r2 right by one; repeat while r2 is not 0. For example: mov r3, #0; loop: and r4, r2, #1; cmp r4, #0; beq skip; add r3, r3, r1; skip: lsl r1, r1, #1; lsr r2, r2, #1; cmp r2, #0; bne loop. A simpler but slower version adds r1 to r3 r2 times.
why use alternate hvh vhv horizontal ver: Each metal layer has a preferred direction, alternating horizontal and vertical between adjacent layers. This lets wires on neighbouring layers cross with just a via, keeps routing regular and dense, reduces coupling capacitance between parallel wires on adjacent layers (they are perpendicular), and simplifies the router's grid and design rules.
with enough routing resources and timing: Yes, but extra buffers increase clock insertion delay and clock power (the clock is the highest-activity net), add more on-chip variation and jitter to the clock path, may increase skew between branches if not balanced, and can change hold timing. The usual goal is the minimum number of buffers that meets skew and transition targets.
how do you fix timing violations on latc: Latch-to-latch paths can use time borrowing: a slow stage can borrow time from the next phase, as long as the data arrives before the latch closes. To fix a real violation, reduce the logic delay (faster cells, restructuring, moving logic across the latch boundary), adjust the clock phases or duty cycle, or retime so each phase has a balanced amount of logic. Check that borrowing does not hide a violation in the following stage, and fix hold with delay buffers.
describe the uvm phases what is the diff: UVM phases: build, connect, end_of_elaboration and start_of_simulation (functions), run_phase (a task), then extract, check, report and final. run_phase is a single task that runs for the whole simulation in every component. main_phase is one of the run-time sub-phases (pre_reset, reset, configure, main, shutdown and their pre/post variants) that run in parallel with run_phase in order, so you can separate reset, configuration and traffic and even jump between phases. Most teams use run_phase only.
what does the virtual keyword do in syst: On a class method, virtual makes the call resolved by the object's actual type at run time (dynamic dispatch), so a derived class's override runs even through a base-class handle. virtual class declares an abstract class that cannot be instantiated. A virtual interface is a handle to an interface instance, which lets class-based testbench code access the DUT's signals.
what formal verification issues have you: Typical issues: state-space explosion, so proofs do not converge (fixed with abstraction, cutting, smaller data widths and assume-guarantee); over-constrained assumptions hiding real behaviour (check with cover properties and vacuity checks); under-constrained inputs giving false counter-examples (add the right protocol assumptions); bounded proofs that are not deep enough; and reset and initial state handling. Describe one real example and how you fixed it.
why use the uvm methodology: UVM provides a standard, reusable structure for testbenches: components, phases, the factory for overriding, config_db for configuration, sequences for stimulus, TLM for communication, and reporting. Teams and vendors share the same methodology, so verification IP plugs in, environments are reused from block to SoC level, and constrained-random coverage-driven verification scales. The cost is boilerplate and a learning curve.
write a systemverilog monitor that captu: The monitor gets a virtual interface, and in a forever loop waits for a valid transaction on the clock (for example @(posedge clk) iff valid), samples the address, read or write and data into a transaction object, and sends it to a checker through a mailbox or analysis port. The checker keeps a model of the memory (an associative array indexed by address): on a write it stores the data, on a read it compares the returned data with the stored value and reports mismatches; it also checks protocol rules such as no X on valid.
write a uvm driver and sequence: Driver: class my_driver extends uvm_driver #(my_item); in run_phase loop forever: seq_item_port.get_next_item(req); drive the fields onto the virtual interface on clock edges; seq_item_port.item_done();. Sequence: class my_seq extends uvm_sequence #(my_item); in task body(), repeat N times: req = my_item::type_id::create("req"); start_item(req); assert(req.randomize() with {...}); finish_item(req);. The test starts it with seq.start(env.agent.sequencer).
what are the ways to optimize timing in: Correct constraints first, then: higher-effort compile, ungrouping hierarchy for cross-boundary optimisation, logic restructuring and retiming, using faster cells (upsizing, lower Vt), buffering high-fan-out nets, path groups and critical-range weighting, register duplication, pipelining at the RTL level, and physical-aware synthesis to get realistic wire delays.
write a bcd converter in verilog: A binary-to-BCD converter is usually written with the double-dabble (shift-and-add-3) algorithm: shift the binary number left one bit at a time into BCD digits, and before each shift add 3 to any BCD digit that is 5 or more. In Verilog: a for loop over the input bits inside always @(*), with an inner loop over the digits doing if (bcd[4k+3 -: 4] >= 5) bcd[4k+3 -: 4] += 3; then bcd = {bcd, bin[i]}. For 8-bit input you need 3 digits (12 bits).
implement a 2d convolution in systemveri: Store the image in a memory, keep the last K-1 rows in line buffers, and use a K x K window register that shifts in one new pixel column per clock. Each cycle multiply the window by the kernel coefficients and add the products with an adder tree, pipelining the multiply and add stages, so you get one output pixel per clock after the buffers fill. Handle borders with zero padding or by skipping outputs, and size the accumulator to avoid overflow.
create a one cell convolutional layer in: A single convolution cell (one output neuron) takes a window of inputs and the kernel weights, computes the multiply-accumulate sum of input x weight over the window, adds a bias and applies an activation such as ReLU (max(0, x)). In Verilog: registers or arrays for the window and weights, a pipelined MAC (or a parallel multiplier array and adder tree), a fixed-point format with saturation, and a valid signal following the pipeline.
if an inverter s input is tied to its ou: It settles at the inverter's switching threshold VM, the point on the transfer curve where Vin = Vout, about VDD/2 for a balanced inverter. Both transistors are in saturation, so a large short-circuit current flows from VDD to ground. This is used to bias inverters as high-gain amplifiers (for example in crystal oscillators), with a feedback resistor.
can a constructor be overridden: No, constructors are not virtual in C++, and in SystemVerilog each class has its own new(). A derived class defines its own constructor, which must call the base constructor first (super.new(...) in SystemVerilog). Because the object type is fixed at construction, there is nothing to override; the factory pattern (as in UVM) is how you get polymorphic construction.
what is the difference between virtual a: A virtual function has an implementation in the base class that derived classes may override. A pure virtual function (pure virtual in SystemVerilog, = 0 in C++) has no implementation in the base class, which must be an abstract (virtual) class, and every non-abstract derived class must implement it. Pure virtual functions define an interface contract.
explain uvm tlm ports: TLM ports let components exchange transactions without knowing each other. Port types: put and get (blocking and non-blocking), peek, and transport; analysis ports implement a one-to-many broadcast with write() for monitors to scoreboards and coverage. Ports (initiators) connect to exports or imps (targets) in the connect_phase; a uvm_tlm_fifo or uvm_tlm_analysis_fifo buffers between them. The sequencer-driver link uses a special seq_item_pull_port.
given a design made of several fifos des: Put an agent (driver and monitor) on each external interface, and monitors on internal boundaries where useful. Build a scoreboard with one reference queue per FIFO path, so expected data and order are checked end to end, plus assertions on each FIFO (no write when full, no read when empty, data order). Stimulus should cover back-to-back writes and reads, full and empty conditions, back-pressure on outputs, different rates in each domain, and reset during traffic; add coverage of fill levels and simultaneous full and empty events.
how do and and or gates work and how are: In CMOS the natural gates are inverting: NAND has parallel PMOS to VDD and series NMOS to ground; NOR has series PMOS and parallel NMOS. An AND gate is built as a NAND followed by an inverter, and an OR gate as a NOR followed by an inverter, so each takes 6 transistors and an extra stage of delay. That is why logic is usually expressed with NAND and NOR.
explain raw waw and war hazards and how: RAW (read after write) is a true dependency: the reader must get the producer's value; in-order pipelines use forwarding and stalls, out-of-order cores wait in reservation stations until the tag is broadcast. WAR (write after read) and WAW (write after write) are name dependencies from register reuse; in-order pipelines that write back in order do not see them, while out-of-order cores remove them with register renaming, and the reorder buffer keeps the final state in program order.
given only the interface of a memory lik: Check reset values and that reads after reset are defined; write and read back each address with patterns such as all zeros, all ones, walking ones and the address as data (to find address aliasing); back-to-back writes and reads, same address read and write in the same cycle; boundary addresses (0 and max) and out-of-range access behaviour; byte enables; and the protocol: latency, ready and valid handshakes, error responses. A reference model with random traffic and coverage completes it.
how are structural hazards handled in ou: Through resource arbitration in the scheduler: instructions only issue when a free functional unit (and a result bus slot) is available, otherwise they wait in their reservation station or issue queue. Designers add multiple copies of busy units, pipeline the units so a new operation can start every cycle, and use separate ports for loads and stores. Full queues (ROB, load and store queues, physical registers) stall dispatch.
how do you balance pipeline stages to me: Measure the delay of each stage, then move logic from the longest stage into neighbouring ones (retiming), split the slowest stage by adding a register, or duplicate logic so it can be computed in parallel. The clock period must be at least the slowest stage plus register overhead (clock-to-Q and setup) and skew, so the goal is equal stage delays. Synthesis tools can retime automatically; check that latency and hazards are still handled.
how many address lines does a given memo: Address lines = log2(number of addressable locations). For a memory of 2^n words you need n lines: 1 K words need 10, 64 K need 16, 1 M need 20. If the memory is byte-addressed but organised in wider words, the lowest bits select the byte within the word. For example a 32 KB memory with 32-bit words has 8 K words, so 13 word-address lines.
describe the mips cpu: MIPS is a classic 32-bit RISC architecture: 32 general-purpose registers (with $0 hardwired to 0), fixed 32-bit instructions in three formats (R, I and J), a load-store design, and simple addressing. The textbook implementation is a five-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) with forwarding, hazard detection and a branch delay slot. It is widely taught and was used in embedded processors, game consoles and routers.
design a frequency multiplier: Common ways: a PLL with a divide-by-N in the feedback path, so the VCO runs at N times the reference; a DLL with edge combining; or, for x2 digital frequency doubling, XOR the clock with a delayed copy of itself so you get a pulse on every edge (the duty cycle depends on the delay). PLLs are preferred for clean, accurate clocks.
explain power gating simulation and the: Power-aware simulation applies the UPF power intent to the RTL: when a domain is switched off, its outputs become corrupted (X) and its registers lose state unless retention is used, so the simulation shows whether isolation, retention and power sequencing are correct. Key UPF concepts: create_power_domain, supply nets and ports, create_power_switch, set_isolation (clamp values and enable), set_retention (save and restore), set_level_shifter, and power states and a power state table describing legal combinations.
for a given rc circuit sketch vout vin o: For an RC low-pass driven by a step, Vout/Vin = 1 - e^(-t/RC): it rises with time constant tau = RC, reaching 63% at one tau and about 99% at 5 tau. If RC = 2 ns, by 10 ns (5 tau) the output has essentially settled. For an RC high-pass the response is e^(-t/RC), starting at 1 and decaying toward 0. Sketch the curve with tau marked, and compare 10 ns with the time constant.
given an anti aliasing filter response w: First, to remove signal and noise above the Nyquist frequency (half the sample rate), which would otherwise alias into the band of interest and cannot be removed afterwards. Second, to limit the noise bandwidth, so out-of-band noise and interferers do not raise the noise floor. The bump (peaking) before roll-off comes from a high-Q filter that gives a sharper transition, at the cost of some ripple and phase distortion in the passband.
given two flops with combinational logic: The minimum cycle time is Tclk >= Tclk-to-Q + Tcomb,max + Tsetup - Tskew (where skew is positive when the capture clock is later), and in practice also plus clock uncertainty or jitter. The hold constraint is Tclk-to-Q + Tcomb,min >= Thold + Tskew. The maximum frequency is 1 / Tclk.
how do you improve ipc with respect to b: Improve prediction accuracy (larger or better predictors, return-address stack, indirect predictors), reduce the mispredict penalty (resolve branches earlier, shorter front end), use a BTB so taken branches do not cost fetch bubbles, and in software use predication or branch-free code. Yes, simple branches (comparisons with zero or equality) can be resolved in the decode stage with a dedicated comparator and early register read, with forwarding into decode, which cuts the penalty to one cycle at the cost of a longer decode path.
how do you tell whether a machine is lit: Write a known multi-byte value to memory and read its first byte: int x = 1; if (*(char *)&x == 1) the machine is little-endian (least significant byte at the lowest address), otherwise big-endian. Or use a union of an int and a char array. Many systems also expose it through compiler macros or CPU registers.
how does time division multiplexing work: Time-division multiplexing shares one link among several streams by giving each a time slot in a repeating frame; faster streams get more slots, and the receiver uses a frame sync to know which slot belongs to which stream. Corner cases: frame alignment and loss of sync, streams whose rates do not divide the frame evenly (needing stuffing bits), all slots used versus idle slots, clock drift between sources (buffers and slips), and reconfiguring the slot allocation without corrupting data.
how would you implement a circular buffe: Use an array, a head index for reads and a tail index for writes, and a count (or keep one slot empty to tell full from empty). Push: if not full, buf[tail] = x; tail = (tail + 1) % N; count++. Pop: if not empty, x = buf[head]; head = (head + 1) % N; count--. With N a power of two, use & (N - 1) instead of %. For a producer and a consumer in an ISR, make the indexes volatile and update each from one side only.
walk through the asic flow: Specification, architecture, RTL design, functional verification, lint and CDC, synthesis with constraints, DFT insertion, equivalence checking, then physical design: floorplan, power grid, placement, CTS and routing, followed by sign-off STA, power and IR drop, signal integrity, DRC, LVS and antenna checks, ECOs, tape-out, fabrication, packaging, test and post-silicon validation.
what is x propagation and why does it ha: X-propagation is how unknown values spread through a design in simulation. It happens when a register has no reset, when there are multiple conflicting drivers, out-of-range array indexes, uninitialised memories or power-down corruption. For example, an if (sel) statement with sel = X takes the else branch in RTL (X optimism) and hides the bug, while the gate-level netlist propagates X (or real hardware picks a random value). Use resets, X-checking assertions and X-propagation simulation modes to find it.
what is the difference between asic and: ASIC design produces a custom chip: you control every gate and wire, so it gives the best performance, power and area, but needs physical design, sign-off and fabrication (high NRE, months of turnaround, no fixes after tape-out). FPGA design maps the logic onto a prefabricated reconfigurable device (LUTs, flops, block RAM, DSPs): fast to iterate and reprogrammable, but slower, more power hungry and more expensive per unit. Coding and timing closure also differ (FPGA-specific primitives, no custom clock trees).
what is the transfer function of a simpl: A VCO's output frequency is linear in its control voltage: f = f0 + Kvco Vc. Phase is the integral of frequency, so in a PLL model the VCO's transfer function from control voltage to output phase is phi(s) / Vc(s) = Kvco / s: an integrator, which adds a pole at the origin to the loop.
what is time borrowing in latches: A latch is transparent for a whole clock phase, so if the logic before it is slow, data can arrive after the opening edge and still be captured before the latch closes. That stage borrows time from the next stage, which then has less time. It lets latch-based designs balance uneven logic across stages, and STA tools compute the borrowed amount and check the next stage.
which metal layers are used for power an: The top, thickest metal layers carry the global power grid and often the main clock spines, because they have the lowest resistance (less IR drop and better electromigration margin) and the clock benefits from low RC delay. Lower and mid layers handle local signal routing. Exactly which layers depends on the technology's metal stack.
with 2 masters and 4 slaves on a bus wha: Check that every request gets exactly one grant and grants are one-hot (only one master owns the bus at a time); a granted master's address decodes to exactly one slave; only the addressed slave responds and drives read data; every transfer gets a response within a bounded time; handshake signals stay stable until accepted; arbitration is fair (no starvation); and invalid addresses get an error response. Write these as SVA with cover properties for each master-slave pair.
explain tomasulo s out of order algorith: Tomasulo's algorithm issues instructions in order to reservation stations. When an instruction issues, it reads available operands or records the tag of the reservation station that will produce each missing one; the register status table marks the destination register with the new tag (renaming), removing WAR and WAW hazards. Stations monitor the common data bus: when a producer finishes, it broadcasts tag and value, and all waiting stations and registers with that tag capture it. Instructions execute when their operands are ready, so they can complete out of order; a reorder buffer is added for in-order commit, precise exceptions and speculation.
explain uvm architecture and flow: The top module instantiates the DUT and interfaces, puts virtual interfaces into config_db, and calls run_test(). The test builds the environment, which builds agents (sequencer, driver, monitor), scoreboards and coverage. In connect_phase, drivers connect to sequencers and monitors to scoreboards through analysis ports. In run_phase, the test raises an objection and starts sequences; items go sequencer to driver to DUT pins; monitors observe and broadcast; scoreboards compare against a reference model; then objections drop, and check and report phases summarise the results.
how do you know your testbench has cover: Measure it: functional coverage tied to the verification plan (every feature, corner case and cross of interesting conditions has a bin), code coverage (line, branch, condition, toggle and FSM) to find untested RTL, and assertion coverage to show properties were exercised non-vacuously. Review the holes, write targeted tests or constraints, and run regressions with many seeds until coverage closes and the bug rate drops. Coverage shows what was tested, not that the checks are right, so review the checkers too.
how does a transaction pass from the gen: The generator (or sequence) creates and randomizes a transaction object and puts it into a mailbox shared with the driver; the driver blocks on mailbox.get(), converts the transaction into pin-level activity through the virtual interface, and may send back a completion through another mailbox or an event. In UVM, the same thing happens through start_item and finish_item on the sequencer and get_next_item and item_done in the driver.
what are the uvm phases and why are they: UVM phases split the simulation into ordered steps that every component follows: build (create sub-components top-down), connect (hook up TLM ports), end_of_elaboration and start_of_simulation (checks and printing), run (the time-consuming test, optionally divided into reset, configure, main and shutdown), then extract, check, report and final. Phasing synchronises all components without manual coordination, and objections decide when the run phase ends.
what data types does systemverilog have: 2-state types: bit, byte, shortint, int, longint; 4-state types: logic, reg, wire, integer, time; real, shortreal and realtime; string; enum, struct and union (packed or unpacked); typedef; arrays: packed and unpacked fixed-size arrays, dynamic arrays, associative arrays and queues; classes, events, mailboxes, semaphores, chandle and virtual interfaces.
why systemverilog how does verilog diffe: SystemVerilog adds what Verilog lacks for large designs and testbenches: classes and OOP, constrained random generation, functional coverage, assertions, interfaces, packages, richer types and always_ff and always_comb for design intent. Verilog differs from C because it describes hardware: everything runs concurrently, there is a notion of time and of clocks, 4-state values (X and Z), and blocking versus non-blocking assignments; C is a sequential program executed instruction by instruction.
convert a piece of rtl logic into a gate: Synthesise it mentally: map each operator to gates or library cells (an adder to full adders, comparisons to XNOR and AND trees, if-else to multiplexers, case to decoders and muxes), each always @(posedge clk) assignment to a flip-flop, and write the netlist as instances of cells (AND2, OR2, MUX2, DFF) with named wires connecting them. Then minimise the logic and check it against the RTL with a truth table or simulation.
describe the synthesis flow: Read the RTL and libraries, elaborate the design into generic logic, apply constraints (clocks, IO delays, exceptions, design rules), then compile: technology-independent optimisation, mapping to library cells, timing and area optimisation, and DFT scan insertion. Generate reports for timing, area, power and constraint violations, write out the netlist and SDC for place and route, and run equivalence checking between the RTL and the netlist.
what is the difference between verilog t: A function returns a value, executes in zero time, cannot contain delays or event controls, cannot call tasks, and needs at least one input; it models combinational calculations. A task can have any number of inputs and outputs, can contain delays, @ and wait (so it can consume simulation time), can call other tasks and functions, and does not return a value directly. Use functions for computations, tasks for timed stimulus.
what is the difference between inter sta: An inter-statement (regular) delay, #5 a = b;, waits 5 time units and then evaluates b and assigns it, so it samples b late. An intra-statement delay, a = #5 b;, evaluates b now, waits 5 time units, then assigns the saved value, so it models a transport delay of the value sampled at that moment. With non-blocking assignments, a <= #5 b; schedules the update 5 units later without blocking the process.
what is the total power dissipation of a: Dynamic power P = alpha C V^2 F, where alpha is the switching activity (the fraction of cycles the node switches, 1 for a clock). The total also includes short-circuit power during transitions and static leakage power: P_total = alpha C V^2 F + P_short-circuit + V I_leak.
which cmos gate is faster nand or and: NAND is faster. In CMOS a NAND is a single inverting stage, while an AND gate is a NAND followed by an inverter, which adds a stage of delay (and area). A NAND is also usually faster than a NOR, because its series transistors are the faster NMOS while a NOR stacks the slower PMOS.
compute the elmore delay of an rc tree w: For an RC tree, the Elmore delay to a node i is the sum over every capacitor k of C_k times the resistance shared between the path from the source to i and the path from the source to k: T_i = sum of R_ik C_k. For a branch, capacitors on the other branch only see the common resistance up to the branch point, while capacitors on the same path see their full upstream resistance. Write the shared resistance for each capacitor and add up the terms.
design a tdm system carrying 120 mbps fr: Use a frame of 12 slots, each carrying 10 Mbps, so 120 Mbps in total. A 10 Mbps stream takes 1 slot per frame, a 40 Mbps stream 4 slots and an 80 Mbps stream 8 slots; any combination with 10X + 40Y + 80Z = 120 fills exactly 12 slots. A slot-allocation table (programmed per configuration) tells the multiplexer which input to select in each slot, a counter steps through the slots, input FIFOs absorb the rate differences, and a frame-sync pattern lets the receiver demultiplex with the same table.
design a circuit that complements the in: Use an XOR gate per bit: out = data XOR enable. When enable = 1, XOR inverts each bit; when enable = 0, it passes the data unchanged. For a bus, replicate enable across the width: assign out = data ^ {N{en}};.
following that design what changes are n: Multiplying Y by G adds a multiplier stage after the adder tree. At 300 MHz, a full multiplier will not fit in one cycle with slow adders, so pipeline it: split it into partial products and an adder tree across several register stages, or use a DSP block, and widen the registers to hold the product (width of G plus width of Y). Balance the pipeline so the extra latency is matched on any parallel paths.
how many multipliers are needed to build: (a + jb)(c + jd) = (ac - bd) + j(ad + bc) needs 4 real multipliers and 2 adders directly. With Gauss's trick it needs only 3 multipliers: k1 = c(a + b), k2 = a(d - c), k3 = b(c + d); then real = k1 - k3 and imaginary = k1 + k2, at the cost of more additions.
implement an fir filter with h0 h4 and h: Use the symmetry to add before multiplying. y = h0 x[n] + h1 x[n-1] + h2 x[n-2] + h3 x[n-3] + h4 x[n-4], with h0 = h4 and h1 = h2, becomes y = h0 (x[n] + x[n-4]) + h1 (x[n-1] + x[n-2]) + h3 x[n-3], so it needs only 3 multipliers instead of 5, plus pre-adders. Linear-phase FIR filters are symmetric for exactly this reason.
with a 1 mhz system clock design the log: With a 1 MHz clock, 5 seconds is 5,000,000 cycles, so use a 23-bit counter (2^23 = 8.4 million). When the car is turned off, clear the counter and start counting; keep the headlights on while the count is below 4,999,999; turn them off when it reaches that value, and stop counting. If the car is turned on again, reset the counter and keep the lights on. A small FSM with states ON, COUNTING and OFF handles it, and the car-off input should be synchronised and debounced.
define a depletion mode mos device: A depletion-mode MOSFET has a channel already present at zero gate voltage, created by implanting dopants under the gate, so it conducts at VGS = 0 and its threshold voltage is negative (for NMOS). Applying a negative gate voltage depletes the channel and turns it off, while a positive voltage enhances it. They were used as loads in NMOS logic and are used in some analog and power circuits.
what is the difference between a micropr: A microprocessor is a general-purpose CPU that relies on external memory, storage and peripheral chips; it is designed for high performance and runs a full operating system. A microcontroller integrates a CPU with flash, RAM, timers, ADCs, communication peripherals and GPIO on one chip; it is designed for dedicated embedded control at low cost and low power.
a right shift and a left shift are equiv: A left shift by n multiplies an unsigned (or two's complement, if no overflow) number by 2^n. A logical right shift by n divides an unsigned number by 2^n, discarding the remainder. For signed numbers, an arithmetic right shift (copying the sign bit) divides by 2^n, rounding toward negative infinity.
which logic gate can be used as a freque: An XOR gate with one input the clock and the other a delayed copy of the clock produces a short pulse on every rising and falling edge, so the output frequency is twice the input frequency. The pulse width equals the delay, so the duty cycle is not 50% unless the delay is a quarter period.
can you measure a 1 ghz square wave with: Not accurately. A 1 GHz square wave has its fundamental at 1 GHz plus odd harmonics at 3, 5 and 7 GHz. A 1 GHz scope (and probe) attenuates the fundamental by about 3 dB and removes the harmonics, so the trace looks like a sine wave of reduced amplitude with slow edges, and the rise time you see is the instrument's (about 0.35 / 1 GHz = 350 ps), not the signal's. Rule of thumb: use a bandwidth of 3 to 5 times the signal frequency, or 0.35 divided by the signal's rise time.
what is the difference between the and o: In a dist constraint, := gives the specified weight to each value in the range, while :/ divides the weight equally among the values in the range. For example, x dist {[0:3] := 2} gives each of 0, 1, 2 and 3 a weight of 2 (total 8), whereas x dist {[0:3] :/ 2} gives the whole range a weight of 2, so each value gets 0.5.
explain the uvm config db how do you con: config_db is a typed, hierarchical database: uvm_config_db #(T)::set(context, "path", "name", value) stores a value for components matching the path, and get(this, "", "name", var) retrieves it in build_phase. To connect the DUT and the testbench, the top module instantiates the interface and the DUT connected to it, then calls uvm_config_db #(virtual my_if)::set(null, "uvm_test_top.*", "vif", my_if_inst); drivers and monitors get the virtual interface and drive or sample the DUT through it.
what is the difference between a uvm obj: A uvm_component is a permanent part of the testbench hierarchy (drivers, monitors, agents, environments, tests): it is created once in build_phase with a name and parent, takes part in phasing, and has TLM ports. A uvm_object is a transient data or configuration object (transactions, sequences, config objects): it has no parent or phases and is created and destroyed freely during the simulation. Both use the factory.
draw a simple nmos current mirror what a: Two NMOS with gates tied together; M1 is diode-connected and carries Iref, so M2 sinks Iout = Iref (W/L)2/(W/L)1. Drawbacks: channel-length modulation makes Iout depend on M2's drain voltage (output resistance only ro), and mismatch causes errors. A cascode mirror (stacking transistors) or a Wilson mirror increases the output resistance by about gm ro and improves accuracy, at the cost of headroom. The output must stay above VGS - Vt (one overdrive) for the simple mirror, or about VGS + Vov for a cascode.
draw a two stage cmos amplifier derive i: Stage 1 is a differential pair with a current-mirror load (gain gm1 (ro2 || ro4)); stage 2 is a common-source amplifier with a current-source load (gain gm6 (ro6 || ro7)). Total DC gain is the product, often 60 to 80 dB, and the output impedance is ro6 || ro7. There are two main poles, one at each high-impedance node, so the amplifier needs compensation: a Miller capacitor Cc between the two stages splits the poles (pushing the first lower and the second higher) for about 60 degrees of phase margin. The Miller capacitor also creates a right-half-plane zero at gm6/Cc, cancelled with a series nulling resistor.
draw the supply current of an inverter o: While the input is low, only leakage current flows. As the input rises past Vtn, both transistors conduct briefly, so a short-circuit current pulse flows from VDD to ground, peaking near the switching threshold. For a rising input the output falls, and the load capacitor discharges through the NMOS to ground, so that current is not drawn from VDD (the supply current is drawn on the opposite, falling-input transition, when the PMOS charges the load). Afterwards the current returns to leakage.
for a single ended cmos differential amp: In a differential pair with a current-mirror load, the input transistor on the diode-connected side of the mirror is the non-inverting input (its current is mirrored to the output), and the transistor at the output node is the inverting input. Small-signal gain Av = gm1 (ro2 || ro4), and output resistance Rout = ro2 || ro4. The dominant pole is at the output, 1/(2 pi Rout CL); the mirror node gives a second, non-dominant pole near gm3/Cmirror, with a left-half-plane zero at about twice that frequency.
given a cmos circuit write its boolean e: Look at the pull-down network: series NMOS transistors mean AND, parallel means OR. Write the pull-down function, and the output is its complement (CMOS gates are inverting). For example, NMOS A in series with the parallel pair B and C gives F = NOT(A AND (B OR C)). Check that the pull-up network is the dual (parallel where the pull-down is series).
two capacitors charged to different volt: Charge flows from the higher-voltage capacitor to the lower one until both reach the same voltage, which is set by charge conservation: Vfinal = (C1 V1 + C2 V2) / (C1 + C2). Some energy is lost in the transistor's resistance (whatever its value). If the transistor is an NMOS whose gate is not high enough, it can stop conducting when the voltage reaches VG - Vt, so the voltages may not fully equalise. This is charge sharing, as in DRAM reads.
two inverters in a loop what is the osci: It does not oscillate. Two inverters in a loop give non-inverting feedback, which is a bistable latch: it settles to one of two stable states and stays there (this is the core of an SRAM cell). An oscillator needs an odd number of inversions, such as a 3-stage ring oscillator with period 2 N td; to increase its period, add stages or load, or starve the current.
what sets the operating frequency of a m: The clock frequency is set by the critical path (the slowest pipeline stage including register overhead), limited further by power and thermal budgets and the supply voltage. Cycles per instruction depend on the design: in an ideal pipeline one instruction completes every cycle (CPI = 1), superscalar cores complete several (CPI below 1), while stalls from cache misses, branch mispredicts and dependencies increase it. Older non-pipelined or microcoded CPUs took several cycles per instruction.
draw the mosfet id vgs and id vds charac: ID versus VGS: zero below Vt, then rising quadratically in saturation (ID = k/2 (VGS - Vt)^2), becoming more linear at high fields in short-channel devices, with a small exponential subthreshold current below Vt. ID versus VDS for several VGS values: rising roughly linearly in the triode region, bending over at VDS = VGS - Vt, and nearly flat in saturation with a slight upward slope from channel-length modulation; higher VGS gives higher curves.
how do you pass a config db setting from: config_db is meant to flow top-down, but any component can call set() with a context and path that a higher-level component will query.
